title: Handing Over an Action Chunk While the World Moves
question: A flow-based VLA plans an action chunk from an observation that is already d steps stale when the chunk arrives; with the policy and the delay fixed, design the rule at the chunk boundary — what to freeze, what to inpaint, how to blend — so execution stays smooth and success survives the delay.
elab: Chunked policies are the norm in current VLAs: the model predicts H future actions from one observation and the robot executes them open-loop. Inference on a large model takes tens to hundreds of milliseconds, so by the time a chunk is ready the observation it was planned from is d control steps old and the robot is partway through the previous chunk. What happens at that boundary — pausing, switching naively, ensembling overlapping chunks, or freezing the actions that will certainly execute and inpainting the rest inside the flow sampler (real-time chunking, Black et al., 2025) — is the closed-loop control problem specific to chunked generative policies, and a 2026 comparison on SmolVLA and LIBERO found that the ranking of the published rules changes with the delay. The task fixes the LIBERO-fine-tuned SmolVLA, imposes the delay, and asks for the chunk-transition rule, measured at three delays on one suite and a fourth condition on another. It matters because a policy that is only correct when the world waits for it cannot be deployed.
readme_settings_line: LIBERO-Spatial, inference delay 2 steps; LIBERO-Spatial, delay 8 steps; LIBERO-Spatial, delay 15 steps; LIBERO-Object, delay 8 steps.
readme_methods_line: naive asynchronous chunk switch, SmolVLA default (Shukor et al., 2025; unmodified starter); fresh chunk executed from step 0, replaying the elapsed actions (null); temporal ensembling, ACT (Zhao et al., 2023; lerobot ACTTemporalEnsembler); IT-RTC soft-mask inpainting as lerobot's RTCProcessor runs it (Black et al., 2025; arXiv:2605.08168 protocol); real-time chunking, the paper's Kinetix reference with full VJP guidance (Black et al., 2025); hard-mask inpainting, RTC's own ablation (Black et al., 2025).

# SmolVLA: What Should Happen at the Chunk Boundary Under Inference Delay?

## Research Question

A flow-based vision-language-action policy predicts a chunk of `H` future
actions from one observation. By the time the chunk has been computed, that
observation is already `d` control steps old and the robot has kept executing
the previous chunk. Given a FIXED policy, a FIXED delay `d`, and the actions
that are already committed, what inference-time rule should produce the next
chunk so that execution stays smooth and task success survives the delay?

## Background

Executing the new chunk as if no time had passed replays stale actions;
switching to it abruptly makes the arm jump between two plans that disagree;
waiting for it stalls the robot. Real-time chunking (RTC; Black, Galliker and
Levine, NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2506.07339) treats the boundary as an inpainting
problem inside the flow sampler: the actions guaranteed to execute during
inference are frozen, and the rest of the chunk is generated by
pseudoinverse guidance to be consistent with them. Follow-up work -- A2C2
(Sendai et al., arXiv:2509.23224), VLASH (arXiv:2512.01031), REMAC
(arXiv:2601.20130), Soft RTC / action-prior denoising (arXiv:2605.25537), and
the 2026 controlled comparison of asynchronous inference methods on SmolVLA
(Agouzoul, arXiv:2605.08168) -- shows that which rule is best depends on how
large the delay is, and that the inference-time methods degrade fastest as
the delay grows. All of those follow-ups change the policy (fine-tuning with
simulated delay, a trained correction head, masked-chunk training). This
task asks the inference-time question only: the policy is
`HuggingFaceVLA/smolvla_libero` (SmolVLA, Shukor et al. 2025,
arXiv:2506.01844, fine-tuned on LIBERO), untouched, and the chunk-transition
rule is yours.

The harness runs the asynchronous protocol of the RTC reference
implementation. The first chunk of an episode is computed synchronously.
After `s` rows of the current chunk have executed, the policy is queried on
the CURRENT observation; during the `d` steps it takes to answer, the robot
executes the next `d` rows of the current chunk (the "committed" actions);
the new chunk, aligned at the query time, then arrives and its rows `d .. s-1`
execute before the next query, with `s = max(d, s_min)`. Your rule is called
once per query. Everything it sees and returns is in the policy's normalised,
padded action space; the harness un-normalises what it executes and drops the
`d` rows that can never execute.

## What You Can Modify

File: `lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/mlsb_custom.py`, the editable
region between the `BEGIN EDITABLE REGION` / `END EDITABLE REGION` markers,
which defines `class ChunkTransitionRule` with

- `reset(batch_size, task)`: called at the start of every batch of episodes of
  one task;
- `plan(ctx) -> Tensor (B, H, A)`: the chunk to execute, aligned at the query
  time.

`ctx` (`mlsb_rtc_runtime.PlanContext`, read-only, same directory) carries the
fixed policy's flow sampler on the fresh observation (`sampler.noise()`,
`sampler.velocity(x_t, t)` -- differentiable w.r.t. `x_t` under
`torch.enable_grad()`, so gradient guidance through the network is possible --
and the shipped 10-step Euler loop `sampler.euler(x1, velocity_fn=None)`); the
previous chunk re-aligned to the query time (`prev_chunk`, with `n_valid` real
rows, of which the first `delay` WILL execute while the policy computes);
`delay`, `horizon`, `step`, `first` (the synchronous first chunk) and `active`.
The rule object persists across the `plan()` calls of one batch of episodes,
so it may keep its own history (earlier chunks, earlier plans). Read
`mlsb_rtc_runtime.py` for the exact protocol and `modeling_smolvla.py` /
`flow_matching.py` / `rtc/modeling_rtc.py` for the fixed sampler and the
shipped RTC processor.

Budget: one `plan()` may spend at most `2 x num_steps` velocity evaluations (a
guided pass with one vector-Jacobian product per step fits; best-of-N
sampling does not; the runtime counts and rejects), and the rule must be an
algorithm on the fixed policy, not a learned corrector: `budget_check.py`
rejects a rule holding more than a token number of trainable parameters. No
access to the network's weights, no training data, no network access.

## Fixed by the Harness

The policy and its checkpoint, the flow sampler and its step count, the chunk
size, the control loop, the imposed delay and execution horizon of each
setting, the environments, their initial states and the episode limits are
all fixed and identical for every rule and every baseline. There are several
evaluation settings that differ in the imposed delay (and one in the
environment), so a rule has to survive a range of delays, not one.

## Metrics

- `success_rate` (scored): fraction of episodes that reach the task's goal
  within the episode limit, per setting; the task score is the geometric mean
  over settings of the per-setting normalised success rate.
- `max_accel` and `boundary_jump` (reported, not scored): the RTC paper's
  jerkiness proxy -- the largest second difference of the executed arm
  command over an episode -- and the mean first difference of the command at
  the chunk-switch steps.

## Baselines

All baselines are ports of a reference implementation, implemented on the
same scaffold and run under the same protocol.

- `naive_async` (the unmodified starter): a fresh chunk from the new
  observation, handed over unchanged; the `d` stale rows are dropped. The
  `NaiveMethodConfig` arm of the RTC reference and lerobot's default
  asynchronous behaviour.
- `delay_unaware` (declared null): executes the fresh chunk from its row 0 on
  arrival, i.e. replays the `d` actions that were meant for the steps that
  already elapsed. Not a method -- the mistake RTC names -- and it must lose.
- `temporal_ensemble`: ACT temporal ensembling (Zhao et al. 2023,
  arXiv:2304.13705, Algorithm 2; lerobot's `ACTTemporalEnsembler`): every row
  executed is the exponentially weighted average, `w_i = exp(-0.01 i)` with
  the oldest prediction weighted most, of every live chunk's prediction for
  that row. The TE baseline of the RTC paper.
- `rtc_soft`: real-time chunking as lerobot implements it
  (`policies/rtc/modeling_rtc.py`, `RTCProcessor.denoise_step`): the
  guidance error `(prev - x1) * W` with an exponential (EXP) soft mask over
  the rows up to the execution horizon, `max_guidance_weight = 5`, and the
  network Jacobian taken as the identity. This is the IT-RTC arm of
  arXiv:2605.08168, which measured it on this checkpoint.
- `rtc_soft_vjp`: RTC exactly as its authors compute it (Eq. 2 of the paper;
  `realtime_action` in the Kinetix reference): the same clipped guidance
  weight, the EXP soft mask over the whole overlap with the previous chunk,
  and the full vector-Jacobian product through the action expert.
- `rtc_hard`: the RTC paper's hard-mask ablation -- the reference guidance
  with binary prefix weights (1 on the committed rows, 0 elsewhere).

Synchronous execution (`d = 0`, the world waits) is the ceiling and is not an
arm. Methods that change the policy (A2C2's trained correction head, TT-RTC,
VLASH, REMAC, Soft RTC) are out of scope by the question's premise; a rule
that reaches what they reach without training is exactly what is asked for.

"""MLS-Bench scaffold: the chunk-transition rule of a real-time chunking policy.

A flow-based VLA (SmolVLA, Shukor et al. 2025, arXiv:2506.01844) predicts a chunk
of H actions from one observation. By the time the chunk is ready the observation
is d control steps old and the robot has kept executing the previous chunk.
Real-Time Chunking (Black, Galliker, Levine, NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2506.07339)
treats the boundary as inpainting inside the flow sampler; follow-up work
(A2C2 arXiv:2509.23224, VLASH arXiv:2512.01031, REMAC arXiv:2601.20130, Soft RTC
arXiv:2605.25537, and the asynchronous-inference comparison arXiv:2605.08168)
shows the best rule depends on the delay. The policy, the delay and the
committed actions are fixed by the harness; the rule is yours.

This module is the ONLY thing you edit. ``mlsb_rtc_runtime.py`` (read-only,
same directory) documents the protocol and calls ``plan`` once per cycle.

Contract
--------
class ChunkTransitionRule:
    reset(batch_size, task)            start of every batch of episodes of one task
    plan(ctx) -> Tensor (B, H, A)      the chunk to execute, aligned at ctx.step

ctx (mlsb_rtc_runtime.PlanContext):
    sampler      the FIXED policy's flow sampler on the fresh observation:
                   .noise() -> (B, H, A) seeded Gaussian noise
                   .velocity(x_t, t) -> v_t, the fixed expert at chunk state x_t
                       and time t in [0, 1] (1 = noise, 0 = actions; a float or a
                       (B,) tensor); differentiable w.r.t. x_t under
                       torch.enable_grad()
                   .euler(x1, velocity_fn=None) -> the shipped 10-step Euler loop
                   .chunk_size H, .action_dim A (padded), .num_steps, .dt
    prev_chunk   (B, H, A) the current chunk re-aligned to the query time; rows
                 [0, n_valid) are the current plan, rows [0, delay) are the actions
                 that WILL execute while the policy computes; the rest is zero
    n_valid      H - horizon
    delay        d: rows [0, d) of your output are never executed
    horizon      s: rows [d, s) of your output execute before the next query
    step         query time within the episode
    first        True on the synchronous first chunk (prev_chunk is all zeros)
    active       (B,) bool, envs still running

Everything is in the policy's normalised, padded action space. A plan may spend
at most 2 x num_steps velocity evaluations (a guided pass with one VJP per step
fits; a best-of-N search does not). The rule must be an algorithm: no trainable
module beyond a token parameter budget (budget_check.py), no access to the
network's weights or to training data. The rule object persists across the
plan() calls of one batch of episodes, so it may keep its own history.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math

import torch
from torch import Tensor

# ================================================================
# FIXED -- DO NOT MODIFY ABOVE THIS LINE
# ================================================================

# ----- BEGIN EDITABLE REGION -----
class ChunkTransitionRule:
    """Naive asynchronous switch (SmolVLA's / lerobot's default): sample a fresh
    chunk from the new observation and hand it over unchanged. The harness drops
    its first `delay` rows (already elapsed) and executes from row `delay`."""

    def reset(self, batch_size: int, task: str) -> None:
        pass

    def plan(self, ctx) -> Tensor:
        s = ctx.sampler
        return s.euler(s.noise())
# ----- END EDITABLE REGION -----

"""Fixed real-time chunking runtime for vla-smolvla-realtime-chunking.

READ-ONLY. Installed into the workspace as
``lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/mlsb_rtc_runtime.py`` by ``edits/mid_edit.py``
and identical for every baseline and every submission; the only thing that
changes is ``mlsb_custom.py``.

The protocol, and why it is what it is
--------------------------------------
The policy is FIXED (a SmolVLA checkpoint fine-tuned on the benchmark; nothing
here trains). It predicts a chunk of ``H`` actions with a 10-step Euler flow
sampler. The harness imposes an inference delay ``d`` (control steps) and an
execution horizon ``s`` and runs the asynchronous protocol of Real-Time Chunking
(Black, Galliker, Levine, NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2506.07339; reference
``Physical-Intelligence/real-time-chunking-kinetix@9296f31d src/eval_flow.py:69-150``:
the synchronous first chunk at :148, ``execute_chunk`` at :71-143 with the
``old[:d] + new[d:s]`` mixing at :119-127 and the shift-by-``s`` re-alignment at
:128-136):

* the first chunk of an episode is computed synchronously (the world waits) and
  executed from row 0;
* every cycle, after ``s`` rows of the current chunk have executed, the policy is
  queried on the CURRENT observation; while it computes (``d`` steps) the robot
  keeps executing rows ``s .. s+d-1`` of the current chunk ("committed");
* the new chunk, aligned at the query time, arrives ``d`` steps later and its rows
  ``d .. s-1`` execute; then the cycle repeats with it as the current chunk.

The editable rule is called once per cycle, at query time, with the current
chunk re-aligned to the query time (``prev_chunk``: rows ``[0, n_valid)`` are the
current plan, rows ``[0, delay)`` are the committed actions that WILL execute
during inference) and a handle on the fixed policy's flow sampler on the fresh
observation. It returns the chunk to execute. Rows ``[0, delay)`` of its output
are never executed -- the schedule, not trust, enforces that the committed
actions cannot be changed.

Everything the rule sees is in the policy's NORMALISED, padded action space
(``max_action_dim`` columns, the first ``action_dim`` real); the harness
un-normalises what it executes. Velocity evaluations are counted per plan and
capped (``MAX_VELOCITY_CALLS``): a guided pass with one VJP per step fits, a
best-of-N search does not (that is the sibling test-time-scaling task's budget).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import math
import time
from typing import Callable, Optional

import numpy as np
import torch
from torch import Tensor

# Velocity evaluations one plan() may spend: 2x the sampler's own step count.
MAX_VELOCITY_CALLS_FACTOR = 2


@dataclasses.dataclass
class PlanContext:
    """What the editable rule receives at every query."""

    sampler: "Sampler"      # the fixed policy's flow sampler on the fresh observation
    prev_chunk: Tensor      # (B, H, A) current chunk re-aligned to the query time; zero-padded
    n_valid: int            # H - s: rows of prev_chunk that are real predictions
    delay: int              # d: rows of the returned chunk that will never execute
    horizon: int            # s: rows d..s-1 of the returned chunk execute
    step: int               # query time (env step index) within the episode
    first: bool             # True for the synchronous first chunk (prev_chunk is all zeros)
    active: Tensor          # (B,) bool: envs still running


class ChunkTransitionRule:
    """Interface the editable rule implements."""

    def reset(self, batch_size: int, task: str) -> None:
        """Called once at the start of every batch of episodes (one task)."""

    def plan(self, ctx: PlanContext) -> Tensor:
        """Return the (B, H, A) chunk to execute, aligned at ctx.step."""
        raise NotImplementedError


class Sampler:
    """The fixed policy's flow sampler, bound to one observation batch.

    ``velocity(x_t, t)`` evaluates the fixed action expert at chunk state ``x_t``
    (B, H, A) and time ``t`` in [0, 1] (1 = pure noise, 0 = actions; a float or a
    (B,) tensor -- the expert takes one time per chunk). It builds an autograd graph if called
    under ``torch.enable_grad()`` with an ``x_t`` that requires grad, so gradient
    guidance through the network is possible. ``euler`` is the shipped sampling
    loop (``lerobot/policies/common/flow_matching.py:euler_integrate`` without
    the RTC hook): ``dt = -1/num_steps``, ``time = 1 + step*dt``, ``x <- x + dt*v``.
    """

    def __init__(self, model, prefix_pad_masks: Tensor, past_key_values, bsize: int, device, generator, max_calls: int):
        self._model = model
        self._prefix_pad_masks = prefix_pad_masks
        self._past_key_values = past_key_values
        self._gen = generator
        self.batch_size = int(bsize)
        self.device = device
        self.chunk_size = int(model.config.chunk_size)
        self.action_dim = int(model.config.max_action_dim)
        self.num_steps = int(model.config.num_steps)
        self.dt = -1.0 / self.num_steps
        # The velocity budget is FIXED by the harness: read-only here (assigning to
        # ``max_calls`` / ``calls`` raises), and the controller re-checks the count
        # against its own copy after every plan().
        self._max_calls = int(max_calls)
        self._calls = 0

    @property
    def max_calls(self) -> int:
        return self._max_calls

    @property
    def calls(self) -> int:
        return self._calls

    def noise(self) -> Tensor:
        return torch.randn(
            (self.batch_size, self.chunk_size, self.action_dim),
            generator=self._gen, device=self.device, dtype=torch.float32,
        )

    def velocity(self, x_t: Tensor, t) -> Tensor:
        self._calls += 1
        if self._calls > self._max_calls:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"velocity budget exceeded: {self._calls} > {self._max_calls} evaluations in one plan()"
            )
        if not isinstance(t, Tensor):
            t = torch.tensor(float(t), dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
        t = t.to(dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
        if t.ndim == 0:
            t = t.expand(self.batch_size)
        elif t.ndim != 1 or t.shape[0] != self.batch_size:
            raise ValueError(
                f"t must be a float or a (B,) tensor (the expert takes one time per chunk); "
                f"got shape {tuple(t.shape)} for B={self.batch_size}"
            )
        if x_t.dtype != torch.float32:
            x_t = x_t.to(torch.float32)
        return self._model.denoise_step(
            prefix_pad_masks=self._prefix_pad_masks,
            past_key_values=self._past_key_values,
            x_t=x_t,
            timestep=t,
        )

    def euler(self, x1: Tensor, velocity_fn: Optional[Callable[[Tensor, float], Tensor]] = None) -> Tensor:
        fn = velocity_fn if velocity_fn is not None else self.velocity
        x_t = x1
        for step in range(self.num_steps):
            t = 1.0 + step * self.dt
            v_t = fn(x_t, t)
            x_t = x_t + self.dt * v_t
        return x_t


def shift_chunk(chunk: Tensor, s: int) -> Tensor:
    """Re-align a chunk by ``s`` rows: rows s..H-1 move to 0..H-s-1, zero-padded
    (Kinetix ``eval_flow.py:128-136``; bt-libero ``eval_libero.py:546-552`` and lerobot's
    ``RTCProcessor.denoise_step`` zero-pad the leftover the same way)."""
    out = torch.zeros_like(chunk)
    if s < chunk.shape[1]:
        out[:, : chunk.shape[1] - s] = chunk[:, s:]
    return out


class RealTimeChunkController:
    """Fixed glue between lerobot's LIBERO vector env, the fixed policy and the rule."""

    def __init__(self, policy, preprocessor, postprocessor, env_preprocessor, env_postprocessor, rule,
                 *, delay: int, horizon: int, seed: int, device):
        from lerobot.policies.common.vla_utils import make_att_2d_masks  # noqa: F401  (import check)

        self.policy = policy
        self.model = policy.model
        self.pre = preprocessor
        self.post = postprocessor
        self.env_pre = env_preprocessor
        self.env_post = env_postprocessor
        self.rule = rule
        self.delay = int(delay)
        self.horizon = int(horizon)
        self.seed = int(seed)
        self.device = torch.device(device)
        self.H = int(policy.config.chunk_size)
        self.real_action_dim = int(policy.config.action_feature.shape[0])
        self.max_calls = MAX_VELOCITY_CALLS_FACTOR * int(policy.config.num_steps)
        if self.delay < 0 or self.horizon < 1:
            raise ValueError("delay must be >= 0 and horizon >= 1")
        if self.horizon < self.delay:
            raise ValueError("horizon must be >= delay (the policy cannot be re-queried before it returns)")
        if self.horizon + self.delay > self.H:
            raise ValueError("horizon + delay must be <= chunk_size, or the current chunk runs out during inference")
        self.plan_seconds = 0.0
        self.n_plans = 0
        self.velocity_calls = 0
        # The policy is FIXED: its weights are fingerprinted once here and checked after
        # every batch, so a rule that reaches the network through the sampler handle and
        # changes a parameter (test-time training, in-place edits) fails the run instead
        # of being scored.
        self._weights_fingerprint = self._fingerprint()

    @torch.no_grad()
    def _fingerprint(self) -> Tensor:
        parts = [p.detach().float().sum() for p in self.policy.parameters()]
        parts += [p.detach().float().abs().sum() for p in self.policy.parameters()]
        return torch.stack(parts).cpu()

    def check_policy_unchanged(self) -> None:
        now = self._fingerprint()
        if not torch.equal(now, self._weights_fingerprint):
            raise RuntimeError("the fixed policy's parameters changed during evaluation; the rule may not modify the network")

    # -- policy plumbing (mirrors SmolVLAPolicy._get_action_chunk / VLAFlowMatching.sample_actions) --
    def _prepare(self, observation: dict, task_descs: list[str]) -> dict:
        from lerobot.envs.utils import preprocess_observation

        obs = preprocess_observation(observation)
        obs["task"] = list(task_descs)
        obs = self.env_pre(obs)
        obs = self.pre(obs)
        return obs

    def _sampler(self, obs: dict, noise_seed: int) -> Sampler:
        from lerobot.policies.common.vla_utils import make_att_2d_masks
        from lerobot.utils.constants import OBS_LANGUAGE_ATTENTION_MASK, OBS_LANGUAGE_TOKENS

        policy, model = self.policy, self.model
        batch = policy._prepare_batch(dict(obs))
        images, img_masks = policy.prepare_images(batch)
        state = policy.prepare_state(batch)
        lang_tokens = batch[OBS_LANGUAGE_TOKENS]
        lang_masks = batch[OBS_LANGUAGE_ATTENTION_MASK]
        prefix_embs, prefix_pad_masks, prefix_att_masks = model.embed_prefix(
            images, img_masks, lang_tokens, lang_masks, state=state
        )
        prefix_att_2d_masks = make_att_2d_masks(prefix_pad_masks, prefix_att_masks)
        prefix_position_ids = torch.cumsum(prefix_pad_masks, dim=1) - 1
        _, past_key_values = model.vlm_with_expert.forward(
            attention_mask=prefix_att_2d_masks,
            position_ids=prefix_position_ids,
            past_key_values=None,
            inputs_embeds=[prefix_embs, None],
            use_cache=True,
        )
        gen = torch.Generator(device=self.device)
        gen.manual_seed(int(noise_seed) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
        return Sampler(model, prefix_pad_masks, past_key_values, state.shape[0], self.device, gen, self.max_calls)

    def _plan(self, obs: dict, prev: Optional[Tensor], step: int, first: bool, active: np.ndarray, noise_seed: int) -> Tensor:
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        sampler = self._sampler(obs, noise_seed)
        B = sampler.batch_size
        if prev is None:
            prev = torch.zeros((B, self.H, sampler.action_dim), dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
            n_valid = 0
        else:
            n_valid = self.H - self.horizon
        ctx = PlanContext(
            sampler=sampler, prev_chunk=prev.detach(), n_valid=n_valid, delay=self.delay,
            horizon=self.horizon, step=int(step), first=bool(first),
            active=torch.as_tensor(active, dtype=torch.bool, device=self.device),
        )
        out = self.rule.plan(ctx)
        if sampler.calls > self.max_calls or sampler.max_calls != self.max_calls:
            raise RuntimeError(f"velocity budget violated: {sampler.calls} evaluations, budget {self.max_calls}")
        if not isinstance(out, Tensor) or tuple(out.shape) != (B, self.H, sampler.action_dim):
            raise RuntimeError(f"plan() must return a tensor of shape {(B, self.H, sampler.action_dim)}, got {getattr(out, 'shape', type(out))}")
        out = out.detach().to(dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
        if not torch.isfinite(out).all():
            raise RuntimeError("plan() returned non-finite actions")
        self.plan_seconds += time.perf_counter() - t0
        self.n_plans += 1
        self.velocity_calls += sampler.calls
        return out

    def _to_env(self, chunk: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        actions = chunk[:, :, : self.real_action_dim].detach()
        if self.policy.config.adapt_to_pi_aloha:
            actions = self.policy._pi_aloha_encode_actions(actions)
        actions = self.post(actions)  # un-normalise; the policy postprocessor moves it to CPU
        return actions.detach().to("cpu", torch.float32)

    # -- one batch of episodes of one task ----------------------------------------------------
    def run_batch(self, env, seeds: list[int], task_descs: list[str], max_steps: int, noise_key: int) -> dict:
        from lerobot.envs.utils import NEW_ROLLOUT_OPTION
        from lerobot.utils.constants import ACTION

        B = env.num_envs
        self.policy.reset()
        self.rule.reset(B, task_descs[0])
        observation, _info = env.reset(seed=list(seeds), options={NEW_ROLLOUT_OPTION: True})
        done = np.zeros(B, dtype=bool)
        ever_success = np.zeros(B, dtype=bool)
        ep_len = np.full(B, max_steps, dtype=np.int64)
        executed: list[np.ndarray] = []
        switch_steps: list[int] = []
        step, base = 0, 0
        cur: Optional[Tensor] = None
        cur_env: Optional[Tensor] = None
        pending = None  # (arrival_step, chunk, chunk_env, base)
        n_queries = 0
        with torch.no_grad():
            while not done.all() and step < max_steps:
                # The policy preprocessor (tokeniser, image normalisation) runs only at a query.
                obs_cache: dict = {}

                def obs():
                    if not obs_cache:
                        obs_cache["obs"] = self._prepare(observation, task_descs)
                    return obs_cache["obs"]

                if cur is None:
                    cur = self._plan(obs(), None, step, True, ~done, noise_key * 1000 + n_queries)
                    n_queries += 1
                    cur_env, base = self._to_env(cur), 0
                elif pending is not None and step == pending[0]:
                    _, cur, cur_env, base = pending
                    pending = None
                    switch_steps.append(step)
                idx = step - base
                if pending is None and idx == self.horizon:
                    prev = shift_chunk(cur, self.horizon)
                    new = self._plan(obs(), prev, step, False, ~done, noise_key * 1000 + n_queries)
                    n_queries += 1
                    new_env = self._to_env(new)
                    if self.delay == 0:
                        cur, cur_env, base = new, new_env, step
                        idx = 0
                        switch_steps.append(step)
                    else:
                        pending = (step + self.delay, new, new_env, step)
                if idx >= self.H:
                    raise RuntimeError(f"chunk exhausted at step {step} (idx {idx} >= H {self.H})")
                action = cur_env[:, idx]
                action = self.env_post({ACTION: action})[ACTION]
                action_np = np.asarray(action.numpy(), dtype=np.float32)
                executed.append(action_np)
                observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action_np)
                successes = _successes_from_info(info, B)
                just = np.asarray(successes, dtype=bool) & ~done
                ever_success |= just
                new_done = np.asarray(terminated) | np.asarray(truncated) | done
                if step + 1 == max_steps:
                    new_done = np.ones_like(new_done, dtype=bool)
                finished_now = new_done & ~done
                ep_len[finished_now] = step + 1
                done = new_done
                step += 1
        self.check_policy_unchanged()
        acts = np.stack(executed, axis=0)  # (T, B, A)
        return {
            "successes": ever_success.tolist(),
            "episode_lengths": ep_len.tolist(),
            "smoothness": smoothness(acts, ep_len, switch_steps),
            "n_queries": n_queries,
            "switches": len(switch_steps),
            "steps": int(step),
        }


def _successes_from_info(info: dict, n: int) -> list[bool]:
    """Mirror of lerobot_eval.rollout's success extraction."""
    if "final_info" in info:
        final_info = info["final_info"]
        if isinstance(final_info, dict):
            is_success = final_info.get("is_success", [False] * n)
            return is_success.tolist() if hasattr(is_success, "tolist") else [bool(is_success)] * n
        out = []
        for item in final_info:
            out.append(bool(item["is_success"]) if isinstance(item, dict) and "is_success" in item else False)
        return out
    if "is_success" in info:
        is_success = info["is_success"]
        return is_success.tolist() if hasattr(is_success, "tolist") else [bool(is_success)] * n
    return [False] * n


def smoothness(acts: np.ndarray, ep_len: np.ndarray, switch_steps: list[int]) -> dict:
    """Per-episode smoothness of the EXECUTED arm command (first 6 dims; the gripper is binary).

    max_accel: max over the episode of the second difference's L2 norm (RTC's jerkiness proxy,
    arXiv:2506.07339 Fig. 7). mean_delta: mean first-difference norm. boundary_jump: mean
    first-difference norm at the chunk-switch steps (nan if the episode ended before one).
    """
    T, B, _ = acts.shape
    arm = acts[:, :, :6]
    max_accel, mean_delta, boundary = [], [], []
    for b in range(B):
        n = int(min(ep_len[b], T))
        seq = arm[:n, b]
        if n >= 2:
            d1 = np.linalg.norm(np.diff(seq, axis=0), axis=1)
            mean_delta.append(float(d1.mean()))
            sw = [t for t in switch_steps if 1 <= t < n]
            boundary.append(float(np.mean([d1[t - 1] for t in sw])) if sw else float("nan"))
        else:
            mean_delta.append(float("nan"))
            boundary.append(float("nan"))
        if n >= 3:
            d2 = np.linalg.norm(seq[2:] - 2 * seq[1:-1] + seq[:-2], axis=1)
            max_accel.append(float(d2.max()))
        else:
            max_accel.append(float("nan"))
    return {"max_accel": max_accel, "mean_delta": mean_delta, "boundary_jump": boundary}

"""
Real-Time Chunking (RTC) implementation for LeRobot.

Based on Physical Intelligence's Kinetix implementation:
https://github.com/Physical-Intelligence/real-time-chunking-kinetix/blob/main/src/model.py#L214
"""

import logging
import math

import torch
from torch import Tensor

from lerobot.configs import RTCAttentionSchedule

from .configuration_rtc import RTCConfig
from .debug_tracker import Tracker

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class RTCProcessor:
    """Real-Time Chunking processor for action chunking policies.

    This class implements RTC techniques including velocity calculation,
    prefix attention, and adaptive chunk processing.
    """

    def __init__(self, rtc_config: RTCConfig, *, trained_mode_supported: bool = False):
        if rtc_config.enabled and rtc_config.mode == "trained" and not trained_mode_supported:
            raise ValueError(
                "RTC mode='trained' requires a PI05-compatible checkpoint trained with "
                "rtc_training_max_delay > 0."
            )
        self.rtc_config = rtc_config

        self.tracker = None

        if rtc_config.debug:
            self.tracker = Tracker(
                enabled=rtc_config.debug,
                maxlen=rtc_config.debug_maxlen,
            )

    # ====================== Tracker Proxy Methods ======================
    def track(
        self,
        time: float | Tensor,
        x_t: Tensor | None = None,
        v_t: Tensor | None = None,
        x1_t: Tensor | None = None,
        correction: Tensor | None = None,
        err: Tensor | None = None,
        weights: Tensor | None = None,
        guidance_weight: float | Tensor | None = None,
        inference_delay: int | None = None,
        execution_horizon: int | None = None,
        **metadata,
    ) -> None:
        """Proxy method to track debug information.

        If tracker is None or disabled, this method does nothing.
        Otherwise, it forwards the call to tracker.track().
        """
        if self.tracker is not None:
            self.tracker.track(
                time=time,
                x_t=x_t,
                v_t=v_t,
                x1_t=x1_t,
                correction=correction,
                err=err,
                weights=weights,
                guidance_weight=guidance_weight,
                inference_delay=inference_delay,
                execution_horizon=execution_horizon,
                **metadata,
            )

    def get_all_debug_steps(self) -> list:
        """Get all debug steps from tracker.

        Returns empty list if tracker is disabled or None.
        """
        if self.tracker is not None:
            return self.tracker.get_all_steps()
        return []

    def is_debug_enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Check if debug tracking is enabled.

        Returns True if tracker exists and is enabled.
        """
        return self.tracker is not None and self.tracker.enabled

    def reset_tracker(self) -> None:
        """Reset the tracker, clearing all recorded steps.

        Does nothing if tracker is None.
        """
        if self.tracker is not None:
            self.tracker.reset()

    # ====================== End Tracker Proxy Methods ======================

    def denoise_step(
        self,
        x_t,
        prev_chunk_left_over,
        inference_delay,
        time,
        original_denoise_step_partial,
        execution_horizon=None,
    ) -> Tensor:
        """RTC guidance wrapper around an existing denoiser.

        This method wraps an original denoising callable that only takes ``x_t`` and
        returns a base denoised velocity ``v_t``. It then applies Real-Time Chunking
        (RTC) prefix guidance using the leftover prefix from the previous chunk.

        Args:
            x_t (Tensor): Current latent/state to denoise. Shape ``(B, T, A)`` or ``(T, A)``.
            prev_chunk_left_over (Tensor | None): Unexecuted prefix from the previous
                chunk. Shape ``(B, T_prev, A)`` or ``(T_prev, A)``. If ``None``, no guidance
                is applied and the method returns ``v_t`` from the original denoiser.
            inference_delay (int): Number of timesteps from the prefix to use for guidance.
            time (float | Tensor): Scalar in [0, 1] indicating normalized time. Must be
                broadcastable with ``x_t``.
            original_denoise_step_partial (Callable[[Tensor], Tensor]): Callable that
                computes the base denoised velocity given only ``x_t``.
            execution_horizon (int | None): Horizon used to build prefix weights. If
                ``None``, defaults to ``self.rtc_config.execution_horizon``.

        Returns:
            Tensor: Guided velocity with the same shape as ``v_t``.

        Notes:
            - If inputs are 2D, a batch dimension is temporarily added and removed at the end.
            - If ``prev_chunk_left_over`` is shorter than the current chunk length ``T``, it is
              right-padded with zeros to match ``T``.
            - Prefix weights are constructed via ``get_prefix_weights(inference_delay, execution_horizon, T)``
              and broadcast to ``(B, T, A)``.
            - Guidance correction is computed via autograd using ``x1_t = x_t + time * v_t`` and
              ``error = (prev_chunk_left_over - x1_t) * weights``.
            - The final guidance weight is clamped by ``max_guidance_weight`` from the config.

        Reference:
            https://www.physicalintelligence.company/download/real_time_chunking.pdf
        """

        # In the original implementation, the time goes from 0 to 1 and
        # In our implementation, the time goes from 1 to 0
        # So we need to invert the time
        tau = 1 - time

        if prev_chunk_left_over is None:
            # First step, no guidance - return v_t
            v_t = original_denoise_step_partial(x_t)
            return v_t

        x_t = x_t.clone().detach()

        squeezed = False
        if len(x_t.shape) < 3:
            # Add batch dimension
            x_t = x_t.unsqueeze(0)
            squeezed = True

        if len(prev_chunk_left_over.shape) < 3:
            # Add batch dimension
            prev_chunk_left_over = prev_chunk_left_over.unsqueeze(0)

        if execution_horizon is None:
            execution_horizon = self.rtc_config.execution_horizon

        # If the previous action chunk is to short then it doesn't make sense to use long execution horizon
        # because there is nothing to merge
        if execution_horizon > prev_chunk_left_over.shape[1]:
            execution_horizon = prev_chunk_left_over.shape[1]

        batch_size = x_t.shape[0]
        action_chunk_size = x_t.shape[1]
        action_dim = x_t.shape[2]

        if prev_chunk_left_over.shape[1] < action_chunk_size or prev_chunk_left_over.shape[2] < action_dim:
            padded = torch.zeros(batch_size, action_chunk_size, action_dim).to(x_t.device)
            padded[:, : prev_chunk_left_over.shape[1], : prev_chunk_left_over.shape[2]] = prev_chunk_left_over
            prev_chunk_left_over = padded

        assert prev_chunk_left_over.shape == x_t.shape, (
            "The padded previous chunk must be the same size as the input tensor"
        )

        weights = (
            self.get_prefix_weights(inference_delay, execution_horizon, action_chunk_size)
            .to(x_t.device)
            .unsqueeze(0)
            .unsqueeze(-1)
        )

        with torch.enable_grad():
            v_t = original_denoise_step_partial(x_t)
            x_t.requires_grad_(True)

            x1_t = x_t - time * v_t  # noqa: N806
            err = (prev_chunk_left_over - x1_t) * weights
            grad_outputs = err.clone().detach()
            correction = torch.autograd.grad(x1_t, x_t, grad_outputs, retain_graph=False)[0]

        max_guidance_weight = torch.as_tensor(self.rtc_config.max_guidance_weight)
        tau_tensor = torch.as_tensor(tau)
        squared_one_minus_tau = (1 - tau_tensor) ** 2
        inv_r2 = (squared_one_minus_tau + tau_tensor**2) / (squared_one_minus_tau)
        c = torch.nan_to_num((1 - tau_tensor) / tau_tensor, posinf=max_guidance_weight)
        guidance_weight = torch.nan_to_num(c * inv_r2, posinf=max_guidance_weight)
        guidance_weight = torch.minimum(guidance_weight, max_guidance_weight)

        result = v_t - guidance_weight * correction

        # Remove the batch dimension if it was added
        if squeezed:
            result = result.squeeze(0)
            correction = correction.squeeze(0)
            x1_t = x1_t.squeeze(0)
            err = err.squeeze(0)

        self.track(
            time=time,
            x1_t=x1_t,
            correction=correction,
            err=err,
            weights=weights,
            guidance_weight=guidance_weight,
            inference_delay=inference_delay,
            execution_horizon=execution_horizon,
        )

        return result

    def get_prefix_weights(self, start, end, total):
        start = min(start, end)

        if self.rtc_config.prefix_attention_schedule == RTCAttentionSchedule.ZEROS:
            weights = torch.zeros(total)
            weights[:start] = 1.0
        elif self.rtc_config.prefix_attention_schedule == RTCAttentionSchedule.ONES:
            weights = torch.ones(total)
            weights[end:] = 0.0
        elif self.rtc_config.prefix_attention_schedule == RTCAttentionSchedule.LINEAR:
            lin_weights = self._linweights(start, end, total)
            weights = self._add_trailing_zeros(lin_weights, total, end)
            weights = self._add_leading_ones(weights, start, total)
        elif self.rtc_config.prefix_attention_schedule == RTCAttentionSchedule.EXP:
            lin_weights = self._linweights(start, end, total)
            lin_weights = lin_weights * torch.expm1(lin_weights).div(math.e - 1)
            weights = self._add_trailing_zeros(lin_weights, total, end)
            weights = self._add_leading_ones(weights, start, total)

        return weights

    def _linweights(self, start, end, total):
        skip_steps_at_end = max(total - end, 0)

        linspace_steps = total - skip_steps_at_end - start

        if end <= start or linspace_steps <= 0:
            return torch.tensor([])

        return torch.linspace(1, 0, linspace_steps + 2)[1:-1]

    def _add_trailing_zeros(self, weights, total, end):
        zeros_len = total - end

        if zeros_len <= 0:

"""Flow-matching sampling primitives shared across policies.

Canonical versions of the beta-distributed timestep sampler and the forward-Euler
denoising loop (with its real-time-chunking hook) that the openpi-derived policies
(pi0, pi05, smolvla, eo1) historically each carried a copy of. All functions are
stateless; adopting them does not affect checkpoints.
"""

from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import torch
from torch import Tensor

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from lerobot.policies.rtc.modeling_rtc import RTCProcessor


def sample_beta(alpha: float, beta: float, bsize: int, device) -> Tensor:  # see openpi (exact copy)
    # Beta sampling uses _sample_dirichlet which isn't implemented for MPS, so sample on CPU
    alpha_t = torch.tensor(alpha, dtype=torch.float32)
    beta_t = torch.tensor(beta, dtype=torch.float32)
    dist = torch.distributions.Beta(alpha_t, beta_t)
    return dist.sample((bsize,)).to(device)


def sample_noise(shape, device) -> Tensor:
    """Standard-normal float32 noise, the flow-matching x_1 sample."""
    return torch.normal(
        mean=0.0,
        std=1.0,
        size=shape,
        dtype=torch.float32,
        device=device,
    )


def sample_time_beta(bsize: int, device, *, alpha: float, beta: float, scale: float, offset: float) -> Tensor:
    """Beta-distributed flow-matching timesteps: ``Beta(alpha, beta) * scale + offset`` (openpi convention)."""
    time_beta = sample_beta(alpha, beta, bsize, device)
    time = time_beta * scale + offset
    return time.to(dtype=torch.float32, device=device)


def euler_integrate(
    denoise_fn: Callable[[Tensor, Tensor], Tensor],
    noise: Tensor,
    num_steps: int,
    *,
    rtc_processor: "RTCProcessor | None" = None,
    rtc_enabled: bool = False,
    inference_delay: int | None = None,
    prev_chunk_left_over: Tensor | None = None,
    execution_horizon: int | None = None,
    hard_prefix: Tensor | None = None,
    hard_prefix_mask: Tensor | None = None,
) -> Tensor:
    """Forward-Euler integration of a velocity field from t=1 (noise) to t=0 (actions).

    This is the openpi sampling loop: ``dt = -1/num_steps``, ``time = 1.0 + step*dt``,
    ``x_t <- x_t + dt * v_t``, with the optional real-time-chunking (RTC) guidance hook
    wrapping the velocity computation and debug tracking after each step.

    Args:
        denoise_fn: Computes the velocity ``v_t`` from ``(x_t, time_tensor)`` where
            ``time_tensor`` is a float32 tensor of shape ``(batch_size,)``. The returned
            velocity must have the same shape and dtype as ``x_t``.
        noise: Initial sample ``x_1`` of shape ``(batch_size, ...)``.
        num_steps: Number of Euler steps.
        rtc_processor: Optional RTC processor. Debug tracking fires whenever it is set and
            has debugging enabled, even if RTC guidance itself is disabled (this mirrors
            the historical per-policy loops).
        rtc_enabled: Whether to route the velocity computation through
            ``rtc_processor.denoise_step`` (requires ``rtc_processor``).
        inference_delay: RTC guidance parameter, forwarded verbatim.
        prev_chunk_left_over: RTC guidance parameter, forwarded verbatim.
        execution_horizon: RTC guidance parameter, forwarded verbatim.
        hard_prefix: Optional clean action prefix to clamp throughout denoising.
        hard_prefix_mask: Boolean mask selecting the values clamped from ``hard_prefix``.
    """
    bsize = noise.shape[0]
    device = noise.device

    dt = -1.0 / num_steps
    x_t = noise
    for step in range(num_steps):
        time = 1.0 + step * dt
        time_tensor = torch.tensor(time, dtype=torch.float32, device=device).expand(bsize)

        if hard_prefix is not None:
            if hard_prefix_mask is None:
                raise ValueError("hard_prefix_mask is required when hard_prefix is provided")
            x_t = torch.where(hard_prefix_mask, hard_prefix, x_t)
            time_tensor = time_tensor[:, None].expand(bsize, x_t.shape[1]).clone()
            time_tensor[hard_prefix_mask[..., 0]] = 0.0

        def denoise_step_partial_call(input_x_t, current_timestep=time_tensor):
            return denoise_fn(input_x_t, current_timestep)

        if rtc_enabled:
            v_t = rtc_processor.denoise_step(
                x_t=x_t,
                prev_chunk_left_over=prev_chunk_left_over,
                inference_delay=inference_delay,
                time=time,
                original_denoise_step_partial=denoise_step_partial_call,
                execution_horizon=execution_horizon,
            )
        else:
            v_t = denoise_step_partial_call(x_t)

        x_t = x_t + dt * v_t

        if hard_prefix is not None:
            x_t = torch.where(hard_prefix_mask, hard_prefix, x_t)

        if rtc_processor is not None and rtc_processor.is_debug_enabled():
            rtc_processor.track(time=time, x_t=x_t, v_t=v_t)

    return x_t

"""Baseline: ACT temporal ensembling (Zhao et al. 2023, arXiv:2304.13705, Alg. 2).

Port of lerobot `policies/act/modeling_act.py:169-260` (`ACTTemporalEnsembler`):
for every row the executed action is the weighted average of the predictions
every live chunk made for that row, `w_i = exp(-m * i)` with `w_0` on the OLDEST
prediction, normalised; `m = 0.01` (ACT's value, lerobot's default
`temporal_ensemble_coeff`). This is the TE arm Real-Time Chunking Sec. 5
compares against ("averages of valid actions are not necessarily valid").
Applied at the query cadence the harness fixes: the rule keeps every RAW chunk
it sampled (not the ensembled outputs, so no prediction is counted twice) and
ensembles them into the returned chunk.
"""
OPS = [
    {
        "op": "replace",
        "file": "lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/mlsb_custom.py",
        "start_line": 60,
        "end_line": 70,
        "content": '''TEMPORAL_ENSEMBLE_COEFF = 0.01   # ACT's m; w_i = exp(-m i), i = 0 on the oldest prediction


class ChunkTransitionRule:
    """ACT temporal ensembling over every live raw chunk."""

    def reset(self, batch_size: int, task: str) -> None:
        self._raw = []   # list of (query_step, raw chunk (B, H, A)), oldest first

    def plan(self, ctx) -> Tensor:
        s = ctx.sampler
        fresh = s.euler(s.noise())
        H = fresh.shape[1]
        q = int(ctx.step)
        if ctx.first:
            self._raw = []
        # forget chunks that no longer predict any row at or after the query time
        self._raw = [(b, c) for (b, c) in self._raw if b + H > q]
        self._raw.append((q, fresh))
        out = torch.zeros_like(fresh)
        wsum = torch.zeros((1, H, 1), dtype=fresh.dtype, device=fresh.device)
        rows = torch.arange(H, device=fresh.device)
        # per row, predictions ordered oldest first get weights exp(-m * 0), exp(-m * 1), ...
        order = torch.zeros(H, dtype=torch.long, device=fresh.device)
        for b, c in self._raw:          # oldest first
            src = rows + (q - b)        # row of chunk `c` that predicts absolute time q + row
            valid = src < H
            w = torch.exp(-TEMPORAL_ENSEMBLE_COEFF * order.to(fresh.dtype)) * valid.to(fresh.dtype)
            out[:, valid] += w[valid][None, :, None] * c[:, src[valid]]
            wsum[:, valid] += w[valid][None, :, None]
            order += valid.long()
        return out / wsum.clamp_min(1e-12)
''',
    },
]

"Understanding Asynchronous Inference Methods for VLA Models" (arXiv:2605.08168),
which is what that paper measured on this policy.

Port of lerobot `policies/rtc/modeling_rtc.py` `RTCProcessor.denoise_step` (:122-254)
and `get_prefix_weights` (:256-303) at the vendored commit fbb811fca9 (byte-identical
at v0.4.2, the release bt-libero pins), driven the way bt-libero drives it
(`TheAyos/bt-libero@cb7a39f6 vlash/eval_libero.py:311-427` patch_policy_with_rtc,
:430-595 rollout_chunked): schedule EXP, max_guidance_weight 5.0 (their
ITRTCMethodConfig, :88), and `execution_horizon = max(d, 10)` passed as the END of
the decay (lerobot semantics: W is 1 on [0, d), decays to 0 at row s, 0 after).
Two things that make this the lerobot variant rather than the RTC paper's reference:
  * the network Jacobian is the identity (lerobot sets `requires_grad` after v_t);
  * the soft mask spans [d, s) instead of the whole overlap [d, H - s).
DEVIATES from lerobot's `RTCConfig` defaults only where bt-libero overrides them
(max_guidance_weight 10 -> 5, LINEAR -> EXP). `rtc_soft_vjp` is the paper's own
algorithm; `rtc_hard` is its hard-mask ablation.
"""
OPS = [
    {
        "op": "replace",
        "file": 'lerobot/src/lerobot/policies/smolvla/mlsb_custom.py',
        "start_line": 60,
        "end_line": 70,
        "content": 'RTC_SCHEDULE = "EXP"
MAX_GUIDANCE_WEIGHT = 5.0   # beta of RTC Eq. 2: Kinetix eval_flow.py:32 (RealtimeMethodConfig), bt-libero eval_libero.py:88


def prefix_weights(start: int, end: int, total: int, schedule: str) -> Tensor:
    """Prefix weights W over the H rows of the chunk: 1 on rows [0, start), a decay on
    [start, end), 0 on [end, total). Port of lerobot `RTCProcessor.get_prefix_weights`
    (+ `_linweights`, `_add_trailing_zeros`, `_add_leading_ones`, modeling_rtc.py:256-303),
    which equals Kinetix `model.py:40-63 get_prefix_weights` row for row: LINEAR is
    (end - i) / (end - start + 1) on [start, end) and EXP multiplies it by expm1(w)/(e - 1)
    (RTC Eq. 5)."""
    start = min(start, end)
    if schedule == "ZEROS":
        w = torch.zeros(total)
        w[:start] = 1.0
        return w
    if schedule == "ONES":
        w = torch.ones(total)

    n = total - max(total - end, 0) - start
    lin = torch.tensor([]) if (end <= start or n <= 0) else torch.linspace(1, 0, n + 2)[1:-1]
    if schedule == "EXP":
        lin = lin * torch.expm1(lin).div(math.e - 1)
    w = torch.cat([lin, torch.zeros(total - end)]) if total - end > 0 else lin
    ones_len = min(start, total)
    return torch.cat([torch.ones(ones_len), w]) if ones_len > 0 else w


def guidance_weight(time: float, max_w: float) -> Tensor:
    """RTC Eq. 2's clipped guidance weight min(beta, (1 - tau) / (tau r_tau^2)) with
    r_tau^2 = (1 - tau)^2 / (tau^2 + (1 - tau)^2), tau = 1 - time (lerobot runs time 1 -> 0).
    Port of lerobot modeling_rtc.py:226-232 == Kinetix model.py:248-250."""
    max_gw = torch.as_tensor(float(max_w))
    tau = torch.as_tensor(1.0 - float(time))
    sq = (1 - tau) ** 2
    inv_r2 = (sq + tau**2) / sq
    c = torch.nan_to_num((1 - tau) / tau, posinf=max_gw)
    return torch.minimum(torch.nan_to_num(c * inv_r2, posinf=max_gw), max_gw)


def guided_velocity(sampler, x_t: Tensor, time: float, prev: Tensor, weights: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """RTC Eq. 2 with the full vector-Jacobian product through the action expert, as the
    authors' reference computes it (Kinetix model.py:236-251 `pinv_corrected_velocity`:
    `x_1, vjp_fun, v_t = jax.vjp(denoiser, x_t)`, `error = (y - x_1) * weights`,
    `pinv_correction = vjp_fun(error)`, `v_t + guidance_weight * pinv_correction`), written
    in lerobot's time convention (time 1 -> 0, x1 = x_t - time * v_t, v = noise - actions,
    hence the minus sign)."""
    with torch.enable_grad():
        x_t = x_t.clone().detach().requires_grad_(True)
        v_t = sampler.velocity(x_t, time)
        x1_t = x_t - time * v_t
        err = ((prev - x1_t) * weights).detach()
        correction = torch.autograd.grad(x1_t, x_t, err, retain_graph=False)[0]
    return v_t.detach() - guidance_weight(time, MAX_GUIDANCE_WEIGHT).to(v_t) * correction


class ChunkTransitionRule:
    """Real-Time Chunking, reference implementation (RTC Eq. 2 with the full VJP, EXP mask over
    [d, H - s))."""

    def reset(self, batch_size: int, task: str) -> None:
        pass

    def plan(self, ctx) -> Tensor:
        s = ctx.sampler
        x_t = s.noise()
        if ctx.first:
            return s.euler(x_t)
        # W = 1 on the committed rows [0, d), EXP decay to 0 at the end of the overlap with the previous plan
        # (row H - s = ctx.n_valid; Kinetix eval_flow.py:83 prefix_attention_horizon), 0 after
        weights = prefix_weights(int(ctx.delay), int(ctx.n_valid), s.chunk_size, RTC_SCHEDULE)
        weights = weights.to(x_t)[None, :, None]
        prev = ctx.prev_chunk.to(x_t)
        for step in range(s.num_steps):
            time = 1.0 + step * s.dt
            v_t = guided_velocity(s, x_t, time, prev, weights)
            x_t = x_t + s.dt * v_t
        return x_t

"""MLS-Bench scaffold: the chunk-transition rule of a real-time chunking policy.

A flow-based VLA (SmolVLA, Shukor et al. 2025, arXiv:2506.01844) predicts a chunk
of H actions from one observation. By the time the chunk is ready the observation
is d control steps old and the robot has kept executing the previous chunk.
Real-Time Chunking (Black, Galliker, Levine, NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2506.07339)
treats the boundary as inpainting inside the flow sampler; follow-up work
(A2C2 arXiv:2509.23224, VLASH arXiv:2512.01031, REMAC arXiv:2601.20130, Soft RTC
arXiv:2605.25537, and the asynchronous-inference comparison arXiv:2605.08168)
shows the best rule depends on the delay. The policy, the delay and the
committed actions are fixed by the harness; the rule is yours.

This module is the ONLY thing you edit. ``mlsb_rtc_runtime.py`` (read-only,
same directory) documents the protocol and calls ``plan`` once per cycle.

Contract
--------
class ChunkTransitionRule:
    reset(batch_size, task)            start of every batch of episodes of one task
    plan(ctx) -> Tensor (B, H, A)      the chunk to execute, aligned at ctx.step

ctx (mlsb_rtc_runtime.PlanContext):
    sampler      the FIXED policy's flow sampler on the fresh observation:
                   .noise() -> (B, H, A) seeded Gaussian noise
                   .velocity(x_t, t) -> v_t, the fixed expert at chunk state x_t
                       and time t in [0, 1] (1 = noise, 0 = actions; a float or a
                       (B,) tensor); differentiable w.r.t. x_t under
                       torch.enable_grad()
                   .euler(x1, velocity_fn=None) -> the shipped 10-step Euler loop
                   .chunk_size H, .action_dim A (padded), .num_steps, .dt
    prev_chunk   (B, H, A) the current chunk re-aligned to the query time; rows
                 [0, n_valid) are the current plan, rows [0, delay) are the actions
                 that WILL execute while the policy computes; the rest is zero
    n_valid      H - horizon
    delay        d: rows [0, d) of your output are never executed
    horizon      s: rows [d, s) of your output execute before the next query
    step         query time within the episode
    first        True on the synchronous first chunk (prev_chunk is all zeros)
    active       (B,) bool, envs still running

Everything is in the policy's normalised, padded action space. A plan may spend
at most 2 x num_steps velocity evaluations (a guided pass with one VJP per step
fits; a best-of-N search does not). The rule must be an algorithm: no trainable
module beyond a token parameter budget (budget_check.py), no access to the
network's weights or to training data. The rule object persists across the
